rows.selection_reason: No prior experiments exist, so the first step is to establish a baseline for rna-only models with a simple encoder (pca_n2000) and singleprofile setting. This will clarify the importance of modalities and basic encoding choices, while keeping other factors (aggregation/fusion) minimal to isolate performance differences.

The existing evidence shows that the RNA-only singleprofile setup (config_001) achieves 0.48 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation method. It balances exploration by addressing key design choices (profile and aggregation) while building on the baseline RNA-only setup. This comparison clarifies whether multiprofile or aggregation improves performance, reducing uncertainty about critical factors without overcomplicating the model.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) for rna_only models. This experiment tests whether switching RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (while keeping multiprofile and avgpool aggregation) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile advantage with exploration of encoder choices, addressing a key design decision with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005, 0.65 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and pca_n2000. This experiment tests whether combining RNA (scvi_n200) with image data (resnet50) in a multimodal setup improves performance. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion while using the best-performing RNA encoder and image encoder, addressing the key uncertainty about whether multimodal approaches can surpass RNA-only models.

Existing evidence shows that for rna_only multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 encoder with avgpool aggregation achieves 0.65 accuracy (config_005). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (while keeping rna_encoder=scvi_n200 and profile_setting=multiprofile) could improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a key design choice, and builds on the strong foundation of config_005 without introducing multiple changes.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models (e.g., config_006) outperform multimodal models (e.g., config_030). This experiment tests the impact of fusion method (weighted vs concat) in multimodal models, isolating a key design choice. It clarifies whether fusion strategy significantly affects performance, even if the model remains below RNA-only benchmarks. This addresses uncertainty about multimodal effectiveness and informs future improvements.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50 encoders, multiprofile settings, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether switching from avgpool to transformer aggregation while maintaining weighted fusion isolates the impact of aggregation methods. It directly compares a critical design choice (aggregation) without altering other components, providing clarity on whether transformer aggregation could further improve performance.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with the more advanced imagenet_vit_l image encoder while retaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could further improve performance. It isolates the impact of the image encoder choice on validation accuracy, building on the strong foundation of config_033 while exploring a key design decision with potential for significant gains.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt while keeping other components identical isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice. It directly compares two key design decisions (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) under the same optimal setup, leveraging strong prior evidence to explore a promising direction efficiently.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 (config_006) outperform scgpt (config_051) in multimodal settings. This experiment tests scgpt in RNA-only with transformer aggregation to isolate the RNA encoder's impact. It clarifies whether scgpt's poor performance stems from its RNA-only capability or multimodal interactions, guiding future multimodal design choices.
